topExamQuestions: Trace the lifecycle of a transaction in a blockchain from signing through broadcast, validation, block assembly, consensus and appending, and explain what a tampered historical transaction forces the network to redo.
Define the key terminologies of blockchain — block, chain, nonce, difficulty, block time, fork, node, wallet and address — and explain how they fit together.
Compare public, private, consortium and hybrid blockchains on permissioning, identity, consensus and governance, and say which type fits a vetted supply-chain consortium.
List the ingredients of a blockchain and explain the role each one plays.
Trace the development of blockchain from centralised databases to permissioned enterprise ledgers, naming the milestones in each era.
Discuss the real-time applications of blockchain, placing each named domain against the problem it solves.
drill: Name the seven steps of a transaction's path.
Sign, broadcast, validate, order, aggregate, agree, append
What is in a block header?
Previous block hash, Merkle root, timestamp, difficulty target, nonce
What does the nonce do?
It is varied until the header hash falls below the target — the search space of proof of work
What is the difference between a node and a wallet?
Node stores and validates the ledger; wallet holds the keypair and signs
What is an address, exactly?
RIPEMD-160(SHA-256(public key)) — 20 bytes, versus a 32-byte public key
How often is difficulty retargeted?
Every 2016 blocks (~2 weeks), to hold the block time near 600 seconds
What happens if a historical transaction is tampered with?
Every block from that one to the tip must be re-hashed and re-mined
How many confirmations for practical finality on Bitcoin?
About 6 — ~60 minutes at a 10-minute block time; fork risk ≈ (1/2)^6 ≈ 1.6%
What two axes fix the type of blockchain?
Who may write (open vs permissioned) and who owns the rules and liability
Where does trust come from on a public chain?
Economics — proof of work or stake, and the cost of rewriting history
Which type is a vetted supply-chain consortium?
Consortium — known members, jointly held rules, shared liability, voting consensus
What does the application do that the ledger does not?
The ledger records; tokens or smart contracts enforce and trigger the workflow
Which ingredient is the Sybil defence?
Mining (or leader election with Sybil-resistant identity in permissioned chains)
Which ingredient prevents backdating?
The timestamp in the block header
Name the three eras of blockchain history.
Open (Bitcoin 2008/09), programmable (Ethereum 2014/15), governed (Fabric 2016)
How is the business case for blockchain measured?
In reconciliation hours removed and disputes avoided
